basic_details.short_information: Holders of a Ph.D. awarded in Wildlife Sciences can apply for 03 Scientist-C posts at the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), Dehradun, an autonomous institution of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. The posts are filled on a Direct Recruitment (D.R.) basis at Pay Level-11 (₹ 67,700 – 2,08,700), and the application, in the Annexure-3 format, must be sent by Registered/Speed Post so that it is received by 02 December 2026 up to 1700hrs (09 December 2026 for applicants from abroad and the listed remote areas).

important_dates.interview_date: To be hosted on the website and intimated to shortlisted candidates

age_limit.details: The age limit is minimum 21 years and maximum 35 years as on the last date for receipt of applications (the application form asks for age as on 02 December 2026). The upper age limit is relaxable for OBC/EWS/SC/ST/PwBD candidates in accordance with instructions/orders issued by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), Government of India, from time to time.

how_to_apply: Fill in the application in the prescribed format given at Annexure-3 (Proforma for Application) of the notice, with a photograph signed across by the candidate.
If the fee applies, prepare a Demand Draft for ₹1,000/- drawn in favour of 'The Director, Wildlife Institute of India', payable at Dehradun.
Attach self-attested copies of the supporting documents listed in the checklist, and sign the checklist.

Candidates already in regular Government service (permanent or temporary, other than casual/adhoc/contract) must attach the declaration at Annexure-4 that they have informed their Head of Office/Department in writing.
Superscribe 'Application for the post of Scientist-C' on the envelope.
Send it by Registered/Speed Post to The Registrar, Wildlife Institute of India, Chandrabani, Dehradun 248001, Uttarakhand, so that it is received by 02-12-2026 up to 1700hrs.
Incomplete applications will be rejected.
The fee is non-refundable and must be deposited via Demand Draft (DD) drawn in favour of 'The Director, Wildlife Institute of India', payable at Dehradun.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The notice advertises 03 posts of Scientist-C at Pay Level-11. The category-wise break-up is: *One (01) post in the OBC category is carried forward from the 2024 recruitment to fill up the backlog vacancy. The application form lets candidates mark the category of post applied for as UR, EWS or OBC-NCL.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Applications are invited from eligible Indian citizens. Area 1: Assessment of wildlife habitats (terrestrial/aquatic), including use of RS & GIS, with at least 02 publications in peer-reviewed journals. Area 2: Ecology or conservation of endangered species, with at least 02 publications in peer-reviewed journals. Area 3: Humanities, Indian Knowledge Systems, or biodiversity conservation, including experience in human-protected area interface & implementation of livelihood extension, with at least 02 publications in peer-reviewed journals. Professional experience in the requisite discipline/area will be counted only after acquiring the mandatory minimum educational qualification and must be supported by credible documentary evidence. The age limit is minimum 21 years and maximum 35 years as on the last date for receipt of applications (the application form asks for age as on 02 December 2026). The upper age limit is relaxable for OBC/EWS/SC/ST/PwBD candidates in accordance with instructions/orders issued by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), Government of India, from time to time. Candidates belonging to OBC-NCL, EWS, SC, ST or PwBD categories may ensure that they fulfil the norms prescribed by the Government of India, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training), and submit a valid certificate in the prescribed format. The notice attaches the OBC certificate format (Annexure-1) and the EWS Income & Asset Certificate format (Annexure-2). The EWS format certifies a gross annual family income below Rs.8 lakh and lists the assets the family must not own. For the discipline-specific eligibility of the post, candidates should check the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: Pay: Level-11 (₹ 67,700 – 2,08,700). Selected candidates will be placed on probation for a period of two years; satisfactory completion of probation is mandatory for confirmation. Candidates holding a degree in Veterinary Science are not entitled to Non-Practicing Allowance (NPA). The headquarters for the post is WII, Dehradun; however, selected candidates are liable to serve anywhere in India as per functional requirements.

content_sections.heading: WII Scientist-C Job Description
content_sections.text: Teaching and training. Extensive field research requiring travel to remote forest interiors, high-altitude areas and islands.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Selection is through screening and shortlisting, a written examination and a personal interview, with a final merit list based on aggregated performance. Applications will be evaluated by a Screening Committee. Fulfilling the minimum eligibility criteria does not automatically entitle an applicant to be called for the test/interview. Shortlisting for interviews will maintain a 1:5 ratio (05 candidates per vacancy), and the institute may at any time increase or decrease this ratio. The written examination comprises subject-specific Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) with 1/3rd negative marking for incorrect answers. Minimum qualifying marks are 50% for UR/EWS/OBC and 40% for SC/ST/PwBD. The Institute's Committee for Recruitment & Selection (ICRS) will assess candidates on academic record, experience in the relevant field, special achievements/awards, teaching experience, publications, and extension/education/institution building. The Written Test carries 70% weightage and the Personal Interview (including presentation) 30%. The final merit list will be prepared on aggregated performance in the written examination and interview. The date(s) of the written test and interview will be hosted on the WII website and intimated to the shortlisted candidates.

faq.question: Q1. How many Scientist-C vacancies has WII advertised?
faq.answer: WII has advertised 03 Scientist-C posts: OBC 01, EWS 01 and UR 01, with the OBC post carried forward from the 2024 recruitment as a backlog vacancy.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date for the WII Scientist-C application?
faq.answer: Applications must be received by 02-12-2026 up to 1700hrs; for applicants residing abroad and from the listed remote areas, the last date is 09-12-2026 up to 1700hrs.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is required for WII Scientist-C?
faq.answer: The essential qualification is a Ph.D. awarded in Wildlife Sciences; experience in one of three listed areas with at least 02 peer-reviewed publications is desirable.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for WII Scientist-C?
faq.answer: Candidates must be minimum 21 years and maximum 35 years as on the last date for receipt of applications, with upper age relaxation for OBC/EWS/SC/ST/PwBD as per DoPT orders.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of WII Scientist-C?
faq.answer: The post is in Pay Level-11 (₹ 67,700 – 2,08,700).

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee and who is exempted?
faq.answer: General, OBC and EWS male candidates pay ₹1,000/- by Demand Draft in favour of 'The Director, Wildlife Institute of India', payable at Dehradun; SC, ST, PwBD and Female candidates are exempted.

faq.question: Q7. How do I apply for WII Scientist-C?
faq.answer: Send the Annexure-3 application with self-attested documents by Registered/Speed Post to The Registrar, Wildlife Institute of India, Chandrabani, Dehradun 248001, Uttarakhand, with 'Application for the post of Scientist-C' written on the envelope.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for WII Scientist-C?
faq.answer: Selection involves screening and shortlisting, a written examination of subject-specific MCQs and a personal interview including presentation, weighted 70% and 30% respectively.

faq.question: Q9. Is there negative marking in the WII Scientist-C written test?
faq.answer: Yes, 1/3rd mark is deducted for each incorrect answer, and the minimum qualifying marks are 50% for UR/EWS/OBC and 40% for SC/ST/PwBD.

faq.question: Q10. Is there a probation period for WII Scientist-C?
faq.answer: Yes, selected candidates will be on probation for two years, and satisfactory completion is mandatory for confirmation.
